question: Can dialog, popover, tooltip, tabs, slider and number-field be rebuilt on Base UI without moving Lumo's public API, and what does the existing accessibility suite say about the result?
verdict: MIXED, and the split is not where the string counts predicted. On ANNOUNCED ENGLISH Base UI wins outright in this batch: React Aria's unreachable `Dismiss` sentinels are gone (0 English on an open dialog, popover, tabs or slider), and slider's `aria-valuetext` — which React Aria discarded at runtime — is now prop-reachable, so the visible number and the spoken number come from the same `formatNumber` call and CANNOT drift. On SEMANTICS Base UI loses one component outright: its Tooltip emits no `role` and no `aria-describedby` anywhere in the package, so the tooltip is text no screen reader is ever pointed at. That defect produces zero English, passes every string-counting measurement in this repository, and is invisible to Lumo's suite because Lumo has no tooltip test. Two further regressions are structural rather than stringy: direction and locale are now separate un-linked props (React Aria derived direction from locale), and React Aria's implicit trigger wiring does not exist, so every trigger is lifted into a `render` prop by hand.

THE_BRIEF_S_TEST_COMMAND_DOES_NOT_EXIST.finding: `packages/ui/src/<name>.test.tsx` exists for NONE of the six components. `pnpm --filter @lumo-ui/ui exec vitest run src/<name>.test.tsx` fails with 'No test files found' for all six, and that is the untouched state of the repository, not a consequence of this rebuild.
THE_BRIEF_S_TEST_COMMAND_DOES_NOT_EXIST.verified: ls of packages/ui/src/*.test.tsx — 28 files, none named dialog/popover/tooltip/tabs/slider/number-field
THE_BRIEF_S_TEST_COMMAND_DOES_NOT_EXIST.actual_layout: Lumo groups tests by DOMAIN, not by component: overlays.test.tsx, controls.test.tsx, hydrated.test.tsx, alert-dialog.test.tsx, command.test.tsx, navigation-menu.test.tsx, menubar.test.tsx, context-menu.test.tsx, provider.test.tsx.
THE_BRIEF_S_TEST_COMMAND_DOES_NOT_EXIST.consequence_for_the_measurement: The conformance bar is real but it is UNEVEN. Coverage was mapped before rebuilding and is reported per component below. Two of the six — tooltip and number-field — have NO test anywhere in the repository, direct or transitive. For those two the suite cannot be the measurement, and the tooltip finding above is exactly what fell through that hole.

method.vendoring: https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/base-vega/<name>.json fetched for all six. FIVE returned 200 (dialog, popover, tooltip, tabs, slider) and were used as the composition reference. `number-field` returned 404 — and so did aria-vega/number-field, and the string 'number-field' does not appear in ui.shadcn.com/r/registry.json at all. shadcn ships no number-field in any style, so Lumo's was hand-written originally and the Base UI rebuild was composed from @base-ui/react/number-field's own .d.ts.
method.adaptation: Public API held fixed; every RAC prop either translated onto a Base UI prop or destructured out and named. Prop-drop lists are per component below.
method.tests: Each suite run individually with `pnpm --filter @lumo-ui/ui exec vitest run src/<suite>.test.tsx --reporter=verbose`. NOT ONE TEST FILE WAS EDITED.
method.typecheck: npx tsc --noEmit in packages/ui — GREEN, 0 errors, with all six rebuilt.
method.extra_probe: A throwaway test file rendered each component under fa-IR and dumped attributes to /tmp; it was DELETED after the numbers below were recorded. It is the only source for the tooltip and number-field rows, which no committed test covers.
method.not_run: pnpm run verify, next build — RAM budget, per brief.

size.note: Lumo's files are majority prose. Both totals are given because the raw one is mostly a measure of how much had to be EXPLAINED, and the code one of how much had to be WRITTEN.
size.where_the_339_lines_went: Almost none of it is composition — Base UI's part trees are the same depth as React Aria's. It is prop translation. Every component now carries an explicit destructuring block naming each React Aria prop that Base UI cannot express, because the alternative is spreading RAC props onto a Base UI element and shipping unknown DOM attributes. slider is the outlier at +15 because its React Aria version was carrying a hand-positioned fill div and an I18nProvider that Base UI's `Slider.Indicator` and `locale` prop replace one-for-one.

suites.note: The strongest single result in this batch. An OPEN Base UI dialog under fa-IR announces zero English and has zero dangling IDREFs — the same bar React Aria met, met by a different engine.

Includes 'names the dialog without drawing anything, and names its ✕'. So DialogHeading→Dialog.Title DOES name the dialog, and Dialog.Close DOES reach an IconButton — both through the trigger-lifting and render-prop wiring this rebuild introduces.

covers: popover (Popover + PopoverTrigger, the only committed test that mounts them)
suites.note: 'an open panel holds LINKS — no role=menu anywhere' passes, so the popover opens, portals and renders under the lifted trigger.

covers: nothing rebuilt — it drives React Aria's Slider directly

failures.test: open-state English > a plain modal dialog is clean; isDismissable on the OVERLAY adds one 'Dismiss'
failures.reading: IT FAILED BECAUSE THE DEFECT IT PINNED IS GONE. The first half of the same test — the plain modal announcing [] — PASSED, so the dialog opens and is clean. React Aria bracketed a dismissable overlay with an internal DismissButton labelled from `@react-aria/overlays`'s `dismiss` string, unreachable by any prop; the test existed to make a RAC upgrade that changed the count go red. Base UI renders no such sentinel — outside-press dismissal is a listener. The assertion is now a floor demanding one English string that no longer exists.
failures.recommended_disposition: If Base UI were adopted this assertion inverts to toEqual([]). NOT CHANGED HERE.

failures.test: open-state English > every open popover carries exactly two unreachable 'Dismiss' labels
failures.reading: Same inversion, one component over. The composition is MenuTrigger/MenuPopover, which a sibling agent rebuilt.

failures.test: open-state English > MenuItem keeps typeahead text and marks submenus with an aria-hidden mirrored glyph
failures.reading: data-has-submenu is null. Not this rebuild's surface.

passing_highlights: 'renders the SAME Persian string visibly and in aria-valuetext' PASSES — output.textContent === aria-valuetext === '۴۰'. This is the assertion the React Aria build needed an I18nProvider to satisfy and could only satisfy indirectly.
'an en-US Slider is Latin, which is the point of the locale prop' PASSES.
'POISON: raw React Aria ships Latin digits' PASSES — it drives RAC directly and is untouched by the rebuild, so the suite's own falsifiability check still fires.

failures.test: Slider > places the thumb from the INLINE-END edge on a Persian page
failures.reading: The test reads `thumb.style.left`, which is the empty string because Base UI does not set `left`. React Aria computed a direction-resolved PHYSICAL offset — 40% of an RTL track became `left: 60%` — so the assertion was pinning RAC's arithmetic. Base UI writes `inset-inline-start: 40%` and lets the browser mirror it. The thumb is placed correctly by a better primitive; the assertion cannot see it. NOTE the test name says INLINE-END and the assertion says `left` — the rebuild satisfies the name and fails the assertion.
failures.recommended_disposition: If Base UI were adopted this becomes `expect(thumb?.style.insetInlineStart).toBe('40%')`. NOT CHANGED HERE.

suites.note: COLLATERAL. alert-dialog.tsx is NOT in this brief's six and was not modified, but it renders `<DialogHeading>` inside a React Aria `<Dialog role="alertdialog">` while its overlay and trigger now come from Base UI.

failures.test: is role=alertdialog, labelled by the Persian title, with zero English spoken
failures.reading: THE ALERT DIALOG LOST ITS ACCESSIBLE NAME. React Aria's `Heading slot="title"` published its generated id through HeadingContext and `useDialog` pointed the dialog's `aria-labelledby` at it. Base UI's `Dialog.Title` writes its id into the Dialog ROOT's store, which only `Dialog.Popup` reads. An RAC `<Dialog>` in between cannot see it. The heading still renders and still reads correctly on screen; only the programmatic name is gone — the exact silent shape this repository's ledger is built around.

failures.test: cancel closes without confirming; confirm runs onConfirm and then closes
failures.reading: AlertDialog closes through the `close` function React Aria hands its Dialog children. That function talks to RAC's OverlayTriggerState, which no longer owns the open state — Base UI's Dialog.Root does. The buttons run, `onConfirm` fires, and the dialog stays open.

suites.why_not_fixed: Fixing it means changing alert-dialog.tsx's engine too, which is outside this brief, or changing its public API, which the experiment forbids. Recorded as the true cost of a PARTIAL migration: dialog.tsx has a consumer that reuses its parts inside a foreign engine, and there is no type error at the seam.

covers: nothing in this brief — it imports menu.tsx only
suites.error: Base UI: MenuRootContext is missing. Menu parts must be placed within <Menu.Root>.
suites.note: Recorded for completeness so the batch's raw numbers are not read as this rebuild's.

announced_strings.method: Rendered under fa-IR in jsdom, every aria-label / aria-roledescription / aria-valuetext / aria-placeholder / title collected. Throwaway probe, since no committed test covers tooltip or number-field.
announced_strings.statement: ZERO. Across all six components there is no English that a Lumo prop cannot close. That is a genuine improvement on the React Aria build, where dialog and popover both emitted `Dismiss` from an internal DismissButton with no prop route at all.

per_component.note: React Aria interpolated the field's label into an English FRAME («Increase <label>»), which is why strings.ts types these as FUNCTIONS of the label. Base UI's are bare verbs with no interpolation, so the required props are now over-specified rather than wrong — `strings.numberField.increase(label)` still yields a correct whole Persian sentence. The React Aria build also applied each label TWICE (root prop + button aria-label) to beat an aria-labelledby RAC would otherwise build; Base UI builds no competing labelledby, so one application suffices.
Base UI's half-localised «۲۰ start range» applies only to RANGE sliders. Lumo's Slider is single-value, so it is not reachable from this API.

per_component.warning: Zero English here is NOT a clean bill of health. See capability_gaps/tooltip-no-aria — the tooltip emits no ARIA at all, which scores perfectly on every string measurement in this repository while being unusable by a screen reader.

capability_gaps.claim: Base UI's Tooltip creates no accessibility relationship between trigger and popup.
capability_gaps.evidence_source: The only `aria-*` attribute anywhere under node_modules/@base-ui/react/tooltip/ is `aria-hidden` on TooltipArrow.mjs:44. There is no `role`, no `aria-describedby`, and no useRole-equivalent in TooltipRoot, TooltipTrigger or TooltipPopup.
capability_gaps.react_aria_behaviour: aria-describedby on the trigger, role=tooltip on the overlay.
capability_gaps.why_it_is_the_worst_kind: It emits zero English, so `no-latin-aria`, the strings sweep and every count in this file score it clean. Lumo has no tooltip test, so nothing goes red. A sighted mouse user sees the tooltip and a screen reader user is never told it exists.
capability_gaps.note: Generating an id and hanging aria-describedby on the trigger would invent a relationship the engine does not have. Left honest per the brief; the file header carries the finding.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria's DialogTrigger/TooltipTrigger wired their first child as the trigger IMPLICITLY, by publishing a ButtonContext carrying onPress, aria-expanded and aria-haspopup. Base UI has no such context and requires a literal <X.Trigger> element or a `render` prop.
capability_gaps.adaptation: React.Children.toArray(children), first child lifted into <X.Trigger render={child} />, remainder rendered after. Preserves `<Trigger><Button/><Overlay/></Trigger>` exactly.
capability_gaps.residual_risk: The lift depends on the first child accepting merged DOM props. It works here only because a sibling agent rebuilt button.tsx on @base-ui/react/button in the same branch; against the React Aria Button it would have had to survive an onClick→onPress boundary. The API is preserved but the mechanism is now positional rather than contextual: a caller who puts the overlay first gets a silently wrong tree, where React Aria's context did not care about order.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria derived reading direction from the locale (useLocale().direction), so one I18nProvider fixed geometry and arrow keys together. Base UI reads direction from its own DirectionProvider, which defaults to 'ltr' and knows nothing about locale or the document's dir.
capability_gaps.consequence_slider: Closed here — Slider mounts a DirectionProvider derived from its own required `locale` prop via direction(). One prop still drives both.
capability_gaps.consequence_tabs: OPEN. Tabs has no locale prop and cannot invent one without changing the API. A Lumo <Tabs> on a Persian page reverses its arrow keys only if the application mounted <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">. Nothing in the type system demands it and nothing renders wrong until a keyboard user presses an arrow.

capability_gaps.claim: Base UI's Dialog.Title calls useDialogRootContext() non-optionally and throws «Base UI: DialogRootContext is missing» outside a Dialog.Root; and where a Root IS present, it publishes the title id into that Root's store, which only Dialog.Popup reads.
capability_gaps.consequence: alert-dialog.tsx renders <DialogHeading> inside a React Aria <Dialog role="alertdialog">. It does not throw (a Base UI Root is above it via DialogTrigger) but the alertdialog element gets no aria-labelledby. Measured: null. React Aria's Heading slot="title" degraded gracefully in the same position.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria read dismissal off the ModalOverlay (opt-in, default off). Base UI puts the inverse control, `disablePointerDismissal`, on Dialog.Root, and outside-press dismissal is ON by default. Lumo's API places the prop on DialogOverlay, which under Base UI is a Portal+Backdrop pair with no route back to the Root.
capability_gaps.consequence: `isDismissable` type-checks and does nothing, and every Base UI dialog in this build is dismissable whether or not the caller asked. The direction of the failure is the dangerous one: an alert dialog that should force a choice can be dismissed by a scrim click.

capability_gaps.claim: The exported cva strings are React Aria's state vocabulary and Base UI does not emit those attributes.

dead_selectors.data-entering / data-exiting: Base UI emits data-starting-style / data-ending-style plus data-open / data-closed. Every enter/exit transition in popoverVariants, tooltipVariants and dialogOverlayVariants/dialogModalVariants is therefore dead; overlays appear instantly.
dead_selectors.data-selected: Base UI marks the selected tab data-active. MEASURED tab attribute list: [type, data-active, data-orientation, data-activation-direction, aria-disabled, tabindex, role, aria-selected, id, data-composite-item-active, data-lumo, class] — no data-selected. So a selected tab renders muted with no accent border.
dead_selectors.data-hovered: Base UI emits no hover attribute (hover is :hover).

capability_gaps.survives: data-orientation and data-disabled. Base UI's generic mapping (internals/getStateAttributesProps.mjs) turns {orientation:'horizontal'} into data-orientation="horizontal" on Root, List, Tab and Panel, so every [data-orientation=…] selector in tabs.tsx still fires.
capability_gaps.not_fixed_because: The brief says swap the engine, not restyle — and popoverVariants is imported by SEVEN components (menu, select, combobox, hover-card, navigation-menu, date-picker, date-range-picker). Forking it desynchronises them.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria read the locale from useLocale(), so one I18nProvider made every number field render and PARSE Persian digits. Base UI has no locale context; `locale` is a per-component prop defaulting to undefined, which Intl.NumberFormat resolves to the runtime locale.
capability_gaps.consequence: A Lumo NumberField formats in Latin digits unless the caller passes `locale` through the spread. Lumo does NOT add a required locale prop here because that would change the public API and this experiment may not. NumberFieldRoot.mjs:110 sets suppressHydrationWarning on the input because server and client locales are expected to disagree, which removes the one signal React would have given.

capability_gaps.claim: Base UI declares Tab.value REQUIRED; React Aria's Tab.id was optional because its collection derived a key from position.
capability_gaps.consequence: A <Tab> written without `id` type-checks against Lumo's unchanged API and reaches Base UI with value: undefined — a tab that can never be selected and whose panel can never match. This is the only `as unknown as` in tabs.tsx and it exists solely to let the API stay as permissive as it was.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria put `delay`/`closeDelay` on TooltipTrigger, per tooltip. Base UI has no delay prop on Tooltip.Root; `delay` exists only on Tooltip.Provider, an app-level grouping component.
capability_gaps.consequence: Both props accepted and dropped. Honouring them would mean one Provider per tooltip, which defeats the grouping the Provider exists for.

capability_gaps.claim: TabList's `items` + `(item: T) => LumoNode` render form has no Base UI equivalent. The generic survives for API parity and the function-child shape is accepted by the type and never invoked. Tab's `href`/`routerOptions` link form is also gone — Base UI's Tab renders a <button> only.
React Aria nested ModalOverlay > Modal > Dialog, so the overlay could be the centring flex container. Base UI's Portal holds Backdrop and Popup as SIBLINGS; the backdrop cannot lay the panel out.
capability_gaps.adaptation: DialogModal centres itself with `fixed inset-0 m-auto h-fit`, applied at the call site so the exported dialogModalVariants stays byte-identical. NOT the vendored shadcn recipe (`top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2`), which is two physical utilities Lumo's lint bans. `inset-0` + `margin:auto` centres on both axes with nothing to mirror.
capability_gaps.flex_classes_now_inert: dialogOverlayVariants still carries `flex items-center justify-center`, which no longer has a child to centre.

wins.claim: The single clearest improvement in this batch. React Aria's useSliderThumb put `'aria-valuetext': state.getThumbValueLabel(index)` as the LAST argument to mergeProps, so a passed aria-valuetext type-checked and was DISCARDED — the quietest possible failure, and the reason the React Aria build had to mount an I18nProvider to influence it indirectly. Base UI (SliderThumb.mjs:244) consults the consumer's getAriaValueText FIRST.
wins.consequence: The visible <output> and the spoken aria-valuetext now come from the same formatNumber call on the same value, so they cannot drift. controls.test.tsx's strictest slider assertion — EQUAL, not merely both non-Latin — passes.

wins.claim: React Aria's two-per-popover and one-per-dismissable-dialog `Dismiss` labels were structurally unreachable — RAC built DismissButton internally with only {onDismiss} and a useLabels call with no other input. Base UI renders no sentinel at all. Three pinned English strings in Lumo's suite are now zero, and the tests fail because they demand them.

React Aria's Placement accepted BOTH `'bottom start'` and `'bottom left'`, and only one mirrored — the defect surface LumoPlacement's Exclude exists to close. Base UI's Side union is 'top'|'bottom'|'left'|'right'|'inline-start'|'inline-end', so the logical spelling is a genuine union member rather than one of two equally-valid options. LumoPlacement still does its job, but it is subtracting from a smaller problem.
wins.note: LumoPlacement is still derived from React Aria's Placement type via a TYPE-ONLY import, because seven still-RAC components consume it. That import is erased at build; popover.tsx carries no RAC runtime.

wins.claim: The React Aria build hand-positioned the fill with insetInlineStart:0 + inlineSize:`${pct}%` — the one place that file turned a raw number into a CSS length. Base UI's Slider.Indicator does it. Thumb placement likewise: measured `inset-inline-start: 40%` rather than a direction-resolved `left: 60%`, so the mirroring is the browser's rather than a computation that can disagree with the fill.

cva_exports_changed: sliderTrackVariants — comment only; class string unchanged
new_exports_added: popover.tsx: PLACEMENT, SideAlign, placementToSideAlign — the LumoPlacement→side/align table. Additive; menu.tsx (a sibling's file) declares a duplicate of the same table, which is recorded here as duplication to collapse if Base UI is adopted.

props_accepted_but_inert.note: Every one is destructured and named in its component with the reason. They are inert rather than removed BECAUSE the API may not change — which is the honest cost: consumer code keeps compiling and quietly stops getting the behaviour.

dialog: level (DialogHeading — Base UI's Title is always <h2>)

unsafe_cast_detail: tabs.tsx Tab — `as unknown as BaseTabs.Tab.Props`, because Base UI requires `value` and Lumo's API leaves `id` optional.

number-field.tsx Root — `as unknown as BaseNumberField.Root.Props`, because React Aria types the component's global DOM handlers against HTMLInputElement while Base UI's Root is a <div> and wraps each handler in BaseUIEvent. Same handlers, same DOM node, mutually unassignable types.
api_preservation.typecheck: GREEN — npx tsc --noEmit in packages/ui reports 0 errors with all six rebuilt.

shared_module_cost.note: Extends the observation already recorded in base-ui-adapter.ts's header.
shared_module_cost.finding: All six components import `attr()` from base-ui-adapter.ts, and number-field also imports asAriaKeyboardEvent. Lumo ships by copy-in, so base-ui-adapter.ts now sits in the dependency closure of every component in this batch as well as button, switch and toggle. popover.tsx additionally becomes a dependency of tooltip.tsx for the PLACEMENT table.

limitations: TOOLTIP AND NUMBER-FIELD HAVE NO COMMITTED TESTS. Their rows come from a throwaway probe that was deleted. Nothing in the repository will notice if either regresses — which is how the tooltip ARIA gap survived to be found by hand rather than by a red build.

NO GATE NUMBERS. packages/gate's RULES were not run over these renders; the brief scoped this to tsc + targeted vitest. `no-latin-aria` would score every component in this batch clean, INCLUDING the tooltip that announces nothing at all.

CONCURRENT AGENTS. button, switch, toggle, menu, select and combobox were being rebuilt in the same working tree during this run. Test failures are attributed per suite above; the 6 counted as sibling-attributable were verified by their error text (MenuRootContext) or by the component under test not importing any of these six files. dialog.tsx's Dialog.Close→IconButton wiring passes BECAUSE button.tsx is Base UI in this tree; against the React Aria Button it is untested.

NO BROWSER. Everything is jsdom. Enter/exit transitions being dead is read from the class strings and Base UI's attribute names, not from an observed frame. Thumb placement is read from the inline style declaration; jsdom computes no layout.
NO SITE BUILD, per the brief. apps/website demos for these six were not type-checked against the rebuilt props, so an inert prop passed by a demo would not have surfaced here.

tests_that_would_need_fixing_in_SOURCE_n: alert-dialog.test.tsx:73 and :96 — the alert dialog genuinely loses its name and its close. alert-dialog.tsx would have to move to Base UI's engine too.
tests_that_must_be_WRITTEN: A tooltip test. There is none, and the most serious defect in this batch lives exactly where the coverage does not.
A number-field test pinning the three announced strings AND the digits of the rendered value.
